name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q01 - Fundamental levels of biodiversity and species proportions

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding fundamental levels of biodiversity and species proportions:

Statement I: Edward Wilson popularised the term 'biodiversity' to describe combined diversity at all levels of biological organisation.

Statement II: Rauwolfia vomitoria displays genetic variation in the potency and concentration of the active chemical reserpine.

Statement III: Animals constitute more than 70 percent of all recorded living species on Earth.

Statement IV: Among animals, insects make up more than 70 percent of the total animal species.

Statement V: The Western Ghats have a greater amphibian species diversity than the Eastern Ghats.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

Fundamental levels of biodiversity and species proportions के संबंध में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एडवर्ड विल्सन ने जैविक संगठन के सभी स्तरों पर संयुक्त विविधता का वर्णन करने के लिए 'जैव विविधता' शब्द को लोकप्रिय बनाया।

कथन II: राउवोल्फिया वोमिटोरिया सक्रिय रसायन रिसरपिन की क्षमता और सांद्रता के संदर्भ में आनुवंशिक भिन्नता प्रदर्शित करता है।

कथन III: पृथ्वी पर अभिलेखित सभी सजीव जातियों में 70 प्रतिशत से अधिक जंतु हैं।

कथन IV: जंतुओं में कीट सबसे समृद्ध वर्गिकी समूह हैं, जो कुल जंतु जातियों के 70 प्रतिशत से अधिक का निर्माण करते हैं।

कथन V: पश्चिमी घाट में पूर्वी घाट की तुलना में अधिक उभयचर जाति विविधता पाई जाती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Evaluation of the sociobiological definition of biodiversity: Sociobiologist Edward Wilson consolidated and popularised the term 'biodiversity' to describe heterogeneous diversity spanning macromolecules to biomes. Thus, this historical definition is accurate.

Step 2:
Evaluation of genetic diversity in Rauwolfia vomitoria: The medicinal plant Rauwolfia vomitoria distributed across Himalayan ranges shows marked variation in the chemical potency and concentration of reserpine. Thus, this genetic variation is accurate.

Step 3:
Evaluation of animal kingdom representation: Global cataloguing indicates that animal taxa constitute more than 70 percent of all described living species. Thus, this taxonomic fraction is accurate.

Step 4:
Evaluation of insect species richness: Among animals, insects represent the largest taxonomic group, accounting for over 70 percent of all animal species. Thus, this entomological figure is accurate.

Step 5:
Evaluation of amphibian diversity in Western Ghats: The Western Ghats harbor significantly greater amphibian species richness than the Eastern Ghats. Thus, this geographical species richness is accurate.

Final Conclusion:
All five statements are correct.

चरण 1:
जैव विविधता की समाजशास्त्रीय परिभाषा का मूल्यांकन: सामाजिक जीववैज्ञानिक एडवर्ड विल्सन ने वृहद्-अणुओं से लेकर बायोम तक जैविक संगठन के सभी स्तरों पर विविधता को दर्शाने के लिए 'जैव विविधता' शब्द को लोकप्रिय बनाया। अतः यह परिभाषा सही है।

चरण 2:
राउवोल्फिया वोमिटोरिया में आनुवंशिक विविधता का मूल्यांकन: विभिन्न हिमालयी श्रेणियों में उगने वाला राउवोल्फिया वोमिटोरिया सक्रिय रसायन रिसरपिन की क्षमता और सांद्रता में आनुवंशिक भिन्नता दर्शाता है। अतः यह जैव-रासायनिक भिन्नता सही है।

चरण 3:
जंतु जगत के प्रतिनिधित्व का मूल्यांकन: वैश्विक अभिलेखों के अनुसार दर्ज की गई कुल जातियों में 70 प्रतिशत से अधिक जंतु हैं। अतः यह वर्गिकी अंश सही है।

चरण 4:
कीट जाति समृद्धि का मूल्यांकन: जंतुओं में कीट सबसे विशाल वर्गिकी समूह हैं, जो कुल जंतु जातियों के 70 प्रतिशत से अधिक का निर्माण करते हैं। अतः यह आंकड़ा सही है।

चरण 5:
पश्चिमी घाट में उभयचर विविधता का मूल्यांकन: पश्चिमी घाट में पूर्वी घाट की तुलना में काफी अधिक उभयचर जातियों की विविधता पाई जाती है। अतः यह भौगोलिक जाति समृद्धि सही है।

अंतिम निष्कर्ष:
सभी पाँचों कथन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q02 - Latitudinal diversity gradients and tropical species richness

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding latitudinal diversity gradients and tropical species richness:

Statement I: Species diversity generally decreases as one moves away from the equator towards the poles.

Statement II: Colombia, located near the equator, has nearly 1,400 species of birds.

Statement III: India, with much of its land area in tropical latitudes, has more than 1,200 species of birds.

Statement IV: Tropical environments are characterized by constant seasonal extremes and severe unpredictable climate fluctuations.

Statement V: The Amazonian rain forest in South America has the greatest biodiversity on earth.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

Latitudinal diversity gradients and tropical species richness के संबंध में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: जैसे-जैसे हम भूमध्य रेखा से ध्रुवों की ओर बढ़ते हैं, जाति विविधता आम तौर पर घटती जाती है।

कथन II: भूमध्य रेखा के निकट स्थित कोलंबिया में लगभग 1,400 पक्षी जातियाँ पाई जाती हैं।

कथन III: भारत में, जिसका अधिकांश भूभाग उष्णकटिबंधीय अक्षांशों में स्थित है, 1,200 से अधिक पक्षी जातियाँ पाई जाती हैं।

कथन IV: उष्णकटिबंधीय पर्यावरण निरंतर मौसमी चरम सीमाओं और गंभीर अप्रत्याशित जलवायु उतार-चढ़ावों की विशेषता वाले होते हैं।

कथन V: दक्षिण अमेरिका का अमेज़न वर्षावन पृथ्वी पर सर्वाधिक जैव विविधता वाला क्षेत्र है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Evaluation of the global latitudinal gradient: Across the planet, species diversity peaks near the equator and diminishes systematically towards temperate and polar latitudes. Thus, this gradient rule is accurate.

Step 2:
Evaluation of avian species richness in Colombia: Positioned close to the equator, Colombia supports extraordinary bird diversity with nearly 1,400 documented avian species. Thus, this avian count is accurate.

Step 3:
Evaluation of bird diversity in India: Because significant portions of India lie within tropical belts, the nation supports over 1,200 species of birds. Thus, this national diversity inventory is accurate.

Step 4:
Evaluation of tropical environmental stability: Tropical environments are actually less seasonal, relatively constant, and predictable, which fosters niche specialization, rather than experiencing severe unpredictable climatic extremes. Thus, describing tropical climates as extremely unpredictable and seasonal is inaccurate.

Step 5:
Evaluation of Amazonian biodiversity dominance: The tropical Amazonian rainforest supports the greatest species richness on Earth, encompassing thousands of vertebrates and millions of invertebrates. Thus, this biodiversity record is accurate.

Final Conclusion:
The first, second, third, and fifth statements are correct, while the fourth statement is incorrect.

चरण 1:
वैश्विक अक्षांशीय प्रवणता का मूल्यांकन: भूमध्य रेखा से ध्रुवों की ओर जाने पर सामान्यतः प्रजाति विविधता लगातार घटती है। अतः यह प्रवणता नियम सही है।

चरण 2:
कोलंबिया में पक्षी समृद्धि का मूल्यांकन: भूमध्य रेखा के निकट स्थित होने के कारण कोलंबिया में लगभग 1,400 पक्षी प्रजातियाँ दर्ज की गई हैं। अतः यह आंकड़ा सही है।

चरण 3:
भारत में पक्षी विविधता का मूल्यांकन: भारत का एक बड़ा भूभाग उष्णकटिबंधीय क्षेत्र में होने के कारण यहाँ 1,200 से अधिक पक्षी जातियाँ पाई जाती हैं। अतः यह राष्ट्रीय विवरण सही है।

चरण 4:
उष्णकटिबंधीय पर्यावरण की स्थिरता का मूल्यांकन: उष्णकटिबंधीय पर्यावरण कम मौसमी, अपेक्षाकृत स्थिर और पूर्वानुमेय होते हैं, न कि अत्यधिक मौसमी चरम सीमाओं या गंभीर उतार-चढ़ावों वाले। अतः यह दावा गलत है।

चरण 5:
अमेज़न वर्षावन की जैव विविधता का मूल्यांकन: दक्षिण अमेरिका का अमेज़न वर्षावन पृथ्वी पर सबसे समृद्ध जैव विविधता वाला पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र है। अतः यह विवरण सही है।

अंतिम निष्कर्ष:
पहला, दूसरा, तीसरा और पाँचवाँ कथन सही हैं, जबकि चौथा कथन गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q03 - Species area relationship principles and mathematical modeling

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding species area relationship principles and mathematical modeling:

Statement I: Alexander von Humboldt observed that within a region, species richness increases with increasing explored area, but only up to a limit.

Statement II: The species-area relationship plotted on normal rectangular coordinates for diverse taxa yields a rectangular hyperbola.

Statement III: On a logarithmic scale, the species-area relationship is described by the linear equation \(\log S = \log C + Z \log A\).

Statement IV: For small regional surveys, the value of the regression coefficient \(Z\) typically ranges from \(0.1\) to \(0.2\).

Statement V: For frugivorous birds and mammals in tropical forests across continents, the regression slope \(Z\) is found to be \(0.15\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

Species area relationship principles and mathematical modeling के संबंध में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: अलेक्जेंडर वॉन हम्बोल्ट ने देखा कि किसी क्षेत्र में अन्वेषण क्षेत्र बढ़ाने पर जाति समृद्धि बढ़ती है, लेकिन केवल एक सीमा तक।

कथन II: विभिन्न टैक्सोन के लिए सामान्य आयताकार निर्देशांकों पर आलेखित जाति-क्षेत्र संबंध एक आयताकार अतिपरवलय (रेक्टेंगुलर हाइपरबोला) देता है।

कथन III: लघुगणक पैमाने पर, जाति-क्षेत्र संबंध को रैखिक समीकरण \(\log S = \log C + Z \log A\) द्वारा दर्शाया जाता है।

कथन IV: छोटे क्षेत्रीय सर्वेक्षणों के लिए, समाश्रयण गुणांक \(Z\) का मान आमतौर पर \(0.1\) से \(0.2\) के बीच होता है।

कथन V: महाद्वीपों के उष्णकटिबंधीय वनों में फलाहारी पक्षियों और स्तनधारियों के लिए समाश्रयण ढलान \(Z\) का मान \(0.15\) पाया गया है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Evaluation of Humboldt's species accumulation principle: Naturalist Alexander von Humboldt established that species richness expands with increasing explored area until reaching an asymptotic threshold. Thus, this ecological principle is accurate.

Step 2:
Evaluation of rectangular hyperbola curve shape: On standard linear coordinates, the mathematical function \(S = C A^Z\) plots as a rectangular hyperbola. Thus, this graphical shape is accurate.

Step 3:
Evaluation of log-log linear transformation: Taking the logarithm of both sides transforms the power curve into the linear form \(\log S = \log C + Z \log A\), where \(Z\) is the regression slope. Thus, this equation is accurate.

Step 4:
Evaluation of regional regression coefficient Z: In localized regional assessments across diverse taxonomic assemblages, the regression coefficient \(Z\) remarkably clusters between \(0.1\) and \(0.2\). Thus, this parameter range is accurate.

Step 5:
Evaluation of tropical frugivore continental slope: For frugivorous birds and mammals evaluated across tropical forests of different continents, the regression slope is steep at \(Z = 1.15\), not \(0.15\). Thus, asserting a slope of \(0.15\) is inaccurate.

Final Conclusion:
The first, second, third, and fourth statements are correct, while the fifth statement is incorrect.

चरण 1:
हम्बोल्ट के प्रजाति संचयन सिद्धांत का मूल्यांकन: अलेक्जेंडर वॉन हम्बोल्ट ने दक्षिण अमेरिकी जंगलों में अन्वेषण के आधार पर पाया कि खोजे गए क्षेत्र के विस्तार के साथ प्रजाति समृद्धि एक सीमा तक बढ़ती है। अतः यह सिद्धांत सही है।

चरण 2:
आयताकार अतिपरवलय वक्र के आकार का मूल्यांकन: सामान्य अक्षों पर समीकरण \(S = C A^Z\) एक आयताकार अतिपरवलय (rectangular hyperbola) प्रदर्शित करता है। अतः यह आलेखीय रूप सही है।

चरण 3:
लघुगणकीय रैखिक रूपांतरण का मूल्यांकन: समीकरण का दोनों पक्षों में लॉग लेने पर रैखिक समीकरण \(\log S = \log C + Z \log A\) प्राप्त होता है, जहाँ \(Z\) रेखा का ढलान है। अतः यह समीकरण सही है।

चरण 4:
क्षेत्रीय स्तर पर समाश्रयण गुणांक Z का मूल्यांकन: सीमित क्षेत्रीय अध्ययनों में विभिन्न वर्गिकी समूहों के लिए ढलान \(Z\) का मान \(0.1\) से \(0.2\) के बीच ही रहता है। अतः यह मान सही है।

चरण 5:
उष्णकटिबंधीय फलाहारी जंतुओं के ढलान का मूल्यांकन: विभिन्न महाद्वीपों के उष्णकटिबंधीय वनों में फलाहारी पक्षियों और स्तनधारियों के लिए \(Z\) का मान \(1.15\) पाया गया है, न कि \(0.15\)। अतः \(0.15\) बताना गलत है।

अंतिम निष्कर्ष:
पहला, दूसरा, तीसरा और चौथा कथन सही हैं, जबकि पाँचवाँ कथन गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q04 - Ecological community stability and Ehrlich rivet analogy

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding ecological community stability and ehrlich rivet analogy:

Statement I: A stable community should show extreme and unpredictable fluctuations in total biomass productivity from year to year.

Statement II: A stable community must be either resistant or resilient to occasional disturbances, whether natural or man-made.

Statement III: David Tilman showed that outdoor plots with greater species richness exhibited less year-to-year variation in total biomass.

Statement IV: In the rivet popper hypothesis proposed by Paul Ehrlich, an airplane represents an ecosystem and rivets represent species.

Statement V: Loss of rivets on the airplane wings symbolizes the extinction of key species that drive major ecosystem functions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

Ecological community stability and Ehrlich rivet analogy के संबंध में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक स्थिर समुदाय को साल-दर-साल कुल बायोमास उत्पादकता में अत्यधिक और अप्रत्याशित उतार-चढ़ाव प्रदर्शित करना चाहिए।

कथन II: एक स्थिर समुदाय को कभी-कभार होने वाले प्राकृतिक या मानव-जनित व्यवधानों के प्रति या तो प्रतिरोधी या पुनरुत्थानशील होना चाहिए।

कथन III: डेविड टिल्मैन ने प्रदर्शित किया कि अधिक जातियों वाले बाह्य भूखंडों ने कुल बायोमास में साल-दर-साल कम भिन्नता प्रदर्शित की।

कथन IV: पॉल एहरलिच द्वारा प्रस्तावित रिवेट पॉपर परिकल्पना में, हवाई जहाज एक पारितंत्र का तथा रिवेट (कीलें) जातियों का प्रतिनिधित्व करती हैं।

कथन V: हवाई जहाज के पंखों के रिवेट्स की हानि उन मुख्य जातियों के विलुप्त होने का प्रतीक है जो प्रमुख पारितंत्र कार्यों को संचालित करती हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Evaluation of community productivity variation: Ecological stability dictates that a community must maintain consistent year-to-year biomass production without extreme swings. Thus, claiming extreme fluctuations characterize stability is inaccurate.

Step 2:
Evaluation of disturbance resistance and resilience: A stable ecosystem possesses resistance against environmental perturbations or resilience to bounce back promptly after disturbance. Thus, this stability criterion is accurate.

Step 3:
Evaluation of Tilman's experimental evidence: David Tilman's field plots demonstrated that elevated species richness dampened annual biomass variations while bolstering overall productivity. Thus, this experimental finding is accurate.

Step 4:
Evaluation of the rivet popper airplane analogy: Paul Ehrlich used an airplane airframe to represent the integrated ecosystem and thousands of structural rivets to symbolize individual species. Thus, this conceptual mapping is accurate.

Step 5:
Evaluation of wing rivets representing keystone species: The wings provide critical lift and flight mechanics; hence, losing rivets on the wings symbolizes losing keystone species driving fundamental ecosystem functions. Thus, this keystone analogy is accurate.

Final Conclusion:
The second, third, fourth, and fifth statements are correct, while the first statement is incorrect.

चरण 1:
समुदाय उत्पादकता में भिन्नता का मूल्यांकन: पारिस्थितिक स्थिरता के अनुसार एक स्थिर समुदाय की कुल उत्पादकता में साल-दर-साल अत्यधिक उतार-चढ़ाव नहीं होना चाहिए। अतः अत्यधिक उतार-चढ़ाव का दावा गलत है।

चरण 2:
व्यवधान प्रतिरोध और पुनरुत्थानशीलता का मूल्यांकन: एक स्थिर जैविक समुदाय प्राकृतिक या मानव-निर्मित व्यवधानों के प्रति प्रतिरोधी या पुनरुत्थानशील होता है। अतः यह स्थिरता का लक्षण सही है।

चरण 3:
टिल्मैन के प्रयोगों के प्रमाण का मूल्यांकन: डेविड टिल्मैन के बाह्य मैदानी प्रयोगों से सिद्ध हुआ कि अधिक प्रजातियों वाले भूखंडों में जैवभार में साल-दर-साल कम भिन्नता होती है। अतः यह निष्कर्ष सही है।

चरण 4:
रिवेट पॉपर सादृश्य का मूल्यांकन: पॉल एहरलिच ने पूरे पारितंत्र की तुलना हवाई जहाज से और प्रत्येक जाति की तुलना हवाई जहाज को जोड़ने वाली कीलों (रिवेट्स) से की थी। अतः यह सादृश्य सही है।

चरण 5:
पंखों के रिवेट्स और मुख्य जातियों का मूल्यांकन: हवाई जहाज के पंखों के रिवेट्स मुख्य (की-स्टोन) प्रजातियों को दर्शाते हैं जो मुख्य पारितंत्र कार्यों का संचालन करते हैं। अतः यह कार्यात्मक व्याख्या सही है।

अंतिम निष्कर्ष:
दूसरा, तीसरा, चौथा और पाँचवाँ कथन सही हैं, जबकि पहला कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, IV and V are correct
Statements I, III, IV and V only are correct
Statements I, II and IV only are correct
Statements II, III, IV and V only are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q05 - Documented extinction history and The Evil Quartet

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding documented extinction history and the evil quartet:

Statement I: The IUCN Red List (2004) documents the extinction of 784 species in the last 500 years.

Statement II: Human colonization of tropical Pacific Islands led to the extinction of more than 2,000 species of native birds.

Statement III: Habitat loss and fragmentation is considered the most important cause driving animals and plants to extinction.

Statement IV: Introduction of the Nile perch into Lake Victoria led to the extinction of over 200 species of cichlid fish.

Statement V: In obligate mutualism, the extinction of one partner invariably leads to the co-extinction of the other.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

Documented extinction history and The Evil Quartet के संबंध में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: आईयूसीएन रेड लिस्ट (2004) पिछले 500 वर्षों में 784 जातियों के विलुप्त होने का दस्तावेजीकरण करती है।

कथन II: मानवों द्वारा उष्णकटिबंधीय प्रशांत द्वीपों के उपनिवेशीकरण से 2,000 से अधिक स्थानीय पक्षी जातियाँ विलुप्त हो गईं।

कथन III: आवास क्षति और विखंडन को जंतुओं और पादपों के विलुप्त होने का सबसे प्रमुख कारण माना जाता है।

कथन IV: विक्टोरिया झील में नील पर्च के प्रवेश से सिकलिश मछलियों की 200 से अधिक जातियाँ विलुप्त हो गईं।

कथन V: अनिवार्य सहोपकारिता में, एक साथी का विलुप्त होना अनिवार्य रूप से दूसरे की सह-विलुप्तता का कारण बनता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Evaluation of IUCN Red List 500-year extinction tally: The IUCN Red List (2004) catalogues 784 documented species extinctions (338 vertebrates, 359 invertebrates, and 87 plants) over the past 500 years. Thus, this baseline record is accurate.

Step 2:
Evaluation of Pacific Island avian extinctions: Anthropogenic colonization of remote tropical Pacific islands precipitated the extirpation of more than 2,000 endemic bird species. Thus, this historical extinction event is accurate.

Step 3:
Evaluation of habitat destruction within the Evil Quartet: Habitat destruction and fragmenting large tracts into small isolated parcels is recognized as the single most lethal driver of modern extinctions. Thus, this ecological ranking is accurate.

Step 4:
Evaluation of invasive Nile perch ecological catastrophe: The predatory Nile perch introduced into East Africa's Lake Victoria eliminated an endemic flock of over 200 cichlid fish species. Thus, this biological invasion consequence is accurate.

Step 5:
Evaluation of obligate co-extinction principle: In obligate mutualistic or host-specific ecological partnerships, the demise of one species inevitably triggers the co-extinction of its dependent counterpart. Thus, this co-extinction dynamic is accurate.

Final Conclusion:
All five statements are correct.

चरण 1:
आईयूसीएन रेड लिस्ट के 500 वर्षों के आंकड़ों का मूल्यांकन: आईयूसीएन (2004) के अनुसार पिछले 500 वर्षों में कुल 784 जातियाँ (338 कशेरुकी, 359 अकशेरुकी और 87 पादप) विलुप्त हो चुकी हैं। अतः यह आंकड़ा सही है।

चरण 2:
प्रशांत द्वीपों पर पक्षी विलुप्ति का मूल्यांकन: मानव द्वारा उष्णकटिबंधीय प्रशांत द्वीपों पर बसने के कारण वहाँ की 2,000 से अधिक स्थानिक पक्षी जातियाँ विलुप्त हो गईं। अतः यह ऐतिहासिक विवरण सही है।

चरण 3:
दुष्ट चतुष्टय में आवास क्षति का मूल्यांकन: प्राकृतिक आवासों का विनाश और विखंडन वर्तमान में जैव विविधता की हानि और प्रजातियों के विलुप्त होने का सबसे मुख्य कारण है। अतः यह क्रम सही है।

चरण 4:
आक्रामक नील पर्च के प्रभाव का मूल्यांकन: पूर्वी अफ्रीका की विक्टोरिया झील में विदेशी नील पर्च के छोड़े जाने से सिकलिश मछलियों की 200 से अधिक स्थानिक जातियाँ समाप्त हो गईं। अतः यह जैविक आक्रमण का विवरण सही है।

चरण 5:
अनिवार्य सह-विलुप्तता के सिद्धांत का मूल्यांकन: अनिवार्य सहोपकारिता में जब एक प्रजाति समाप्त होती है, तो उस पर आश्रित दूसरी प्रजाति भी अनिवार्य रूप से विलुप्त हो जाती है। अतः यह सिद्धांत सही है।

अंतिम निष्कर्ष:
सभी पाँचों कथन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_STATEMENT_Q06 - In situ and ex situ biodiversity conservation approaches

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding in situ and ex situ biodiversity conservation approaches:

Statement I: Biodiversity hotspots are characterized by exceptionally high levels of species richness and a high degree of endemism.

Statement II: All 34 biodiversity hotspots put together cover less than 2 percent of the Earth's land area.

Statement III: Three biodiversity hotspots—Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, and Himalaya—cover India's high biodiversity regions.

Statement IV: Sacred groves represent an ex-situ conservation strategy where rare plants are cultivated in botanical gardens.

Statement V: Cryopreservation allows gametes of threatened species to be preserved in viable and fertile condition for long periods.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

In situ and ex situ biodiversity conservation approaches के संबंध में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: जैव विविधता हॉटस्पॉट असाधारण रूप से उच्च स्तर की जाति समृद्धि और उच्च स्थानिक स्थिति (एंडेमिज्म) की विशेषता रखते हैं।

कथन II: संसार के सभी 34 जैव विविधता हॉटस्पॉट मिलकर पृथ्वी के कुल भूभाग के 2 प्रतिशत से भी कम क्षेत्र को आच्छादित करते हैं।

कथन III: तीन जैव विविधता हॉटस्पॉट—पश्चिमी घाट और श्रीलंका, इंडो-बर्मा तथा हिमालय—भारत के उच्च जैव विविधता वाले क्षेत्रों को कवर करते हैं।

कथन IV: पवित्र उपवन एक बाह्य-स्थाने (ex-situ) संरक्षण रणनीति का प्रतिनिधित्व करते हैं जहाँ दुर्लभ पादपों को वानस्पतिक उद्यानों में उगाया जाता है।

कथन V: युग्मकों का हिमपरिरक्षण (क्रायोप्रिजर्वेशन) संकटापन्न जातियों के युग्मकों को लंबे समय तक जीवनक्षम और जननक्षम स्थिति में रखने की अनुमति देता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Evaluation of biodiversity hotspot criteria: Designated hotspots are regions defined by extraordinary species richness alongside high endemism, where species are restricted strictly to that geography. Thus, this definition is accurate.

Step 2:
Evaluation of total terrestrial area occupied by hotspots: Despite harboring the vast majority of endemic global biota, all 34 hotspots together occupy less than 2 percent of Earth's land surface. Thus, this terrestrial coverage is accurate.

Step 3:
Evaluation of hotspots spanning India: Three internationally designated hotspots extend across Indian borders: Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, and Himalaya. Thus, this biogeographical attribution is accurate.

Step 4:
Evaluation of sacred groves conservation modality: Sacred groves are intact natural forest tracts protected in place by indigenous cultural traditions, representing an in-situ conservation mechanism rather than an ex-situ botanical garden method. Thus, classifying sacred groves as ex-situ is inaccurate.

Step 5:
Evaluation of cryopreservation biotechnology: Cryogenic freezing in liquid nitrogen (-196 °C) enables viable, long-term ex-situ preservation of reproductive gametes from endangered species. Thus, this biotechnological description is accurate.

Final Conclusion:
The first, second, third, and fifth statements are correct, while the fourth statement is incorrect.

चरण 1:
जैव विविधता हॉटस्पॉट के मानदंडों का मूल्यांकन: हॉटस्पॉट वे क्षेत्र हैं जहाँ अत्यधिक जाति समृद्धि और उच्च स्तर की स्थानिकता (endemism) पाई जाती है, जहाँ की प्रजातियाँ अन्यत्र कहीं नहीं पाई जातीं। अतः यह परिभाषा सही है।

चरण 2:
हॉटस्पॉटों के कुल भू-क्षेत्र का मूल्यांकन: संसार के सभी 34 हॉटस्पॉट मिलकर पृथ्वी के कुल स्थल क्षेत्र के 2 प्रतिशत से भी कम भूभाग को घेरते हैं। अतः यह भौगोलिक प्रतिशत सही है।

चरण 3:
भारत से संबंधित हॉटस्पॉटों का मूल्यांकन: भारत के असाधारण रूप से समृद्ध जैव विविधता वाले क्षेत्रों को तीन हॉटस्पॉट कवर करते हैं: पश्चिमी घाट और श्रीलंका, इंडो-बर्मा तथा हिमालय। अतः यह विवरण सही है।

चरण 4:
पवित्र उपवनों की संरक्षण पद्धति का मूल्यांकन: पवित्र उपवन धार्मिक परंपराओं द्वारा जंगलों के प्राकृतिक भागों को सुरक्षित रखने की पद्धति है, जो स्व-स्थाने (in-situ) संरक्षण के अंतर्गत आते हैं, न कि वानस्पतिक उद्यान जैसे बाह्य-स्थाने में। अतः पवित्र उपवनों को बाह्य-स्थाने कहना गलत है।

चरण 5:
क्रायोप्रिजर्वेशन (हिमपरिरक्षण) तकनीक का मूल्यांकन: क्रायोप्रिजर्वेशन तकनीक द्वारा संकटापन्न प्रजातियों के युग्मकों को अत्यंत कम तापमान पर लंबे समय तक सुरक्षित और जननक्षम रखा जा सकता है। अतः यह तकनीकी विवरण सही है।

अंतिम निष्कर्ष:
पहला, दूसरा, तीसरा और पाँचवाँ कथन सही हैं, जबकि चौथा कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, IV and V are correct
Statements I, II, III and V only are correct
Statements II, III, IV and V only are correct
Statements I, III and IV only are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MATCH_LIST_Q01 - Recently extinct organisms and their geographic origins

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Extinct Organism) List II (Geographic Location)
A. Dodo I. Africa
B. Quagga II. Russia
C. Thylacine III. Mauritius
D. Steller's sea cow IV. Australia

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Extinction history of the Dodo
The dodo was a flightless bird endemic to the island of Mauritius that succumbed to extinction due to human exploitation and introduced predators.

Step 2: Extinction history of the Quagga
The quagga was a distinct subspecies of plains zebra native to Africa that was driven to extinction in the late nineteenth century through over-hunting.

Step 3: Extinction history of the Thylacine
The thylacine, also known as the Tasmanian wolf or tiger, was a carnivorous marsupial native to Australia that went extinct during the twentieth century.

Step 4: Extinction history of Steller's sea cow
Steller's sea cow was an enormous herbivorous marine mammal native to the Commander Islands near the coast of Russia that was driven to extinction within three decades of discovery due to over-harvesting.

Step 5: Final conceptual conclusion
Matching each extinct organism with its native geographic region establishes that the dodo corresponds to Mauritius, the quagga corresponds to Africa, the thylacine corresponds to Australia, and Steller's sea cow corresponds to Russia. Therefore, the correct combination pairs A with III, B with I, C with IV, and D with II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MATCH_LIST_Q02 - In situ and ex situ conservation methods

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Conservation Strategy) List II (Description or Mode)
A. Biosphere reserve I. Ex situ conservation using low-temperature gamete preservation
B. Zoological park II. In situ legal protection of entire ecosystems and natural habitats
C. Sacred grove III. Ex situ maintenance of wild animals under human care in enclosures
D. Cryopreservation IV. In situ traditional protection of forest tracts based on cultural veneration

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Characterize biosphere reserves
A biosphere reserve is a large, legally protected natural area designed for in situ conservation where the entire ecosystem and its biological communities are protected on site.

Step 2: Characterize zoological parks
A zoological park is an off-site facility where threatened and wild animals are taken out of their natural habitats and housed in protective enclosures under human care, representing ex situ conservation.

Step 3: Characterize sacred groves
Sacred groves are tracts of natural forest set aside and venerated by indigenous communities due to religious and cultural traditions, serving as in situ refuges for native plants and wildlife.

Step 4: Characterize cryopreservation
Cryopreservation is an advanced ex situ technique where gametes of threatened species are preserved in liquid nitrogen at extremely low temperatures in viable and fertile conditions for long periods.

Step 5: Final conceptual conclusion
Evaluating each conservation strategy reveals that the biosphere reserve aligns with in situ legal protection of entire ecosystems, the zoological park aligns with ex situ maintenance of wild animals in enclosures, the sacred grove aligns with in situ traditional protection of forest tracts, and cryopreservation aligns with ex situ gamete preservation at low temperatures. Therefore, the correct combination pairs A with II, B with III, C with IV, and D with I.

answer.text: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MATCH_LIST_Q03 - Levels of biodiversity and their characteristic examples

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Biological Observation) List II (Level of Diversity)
A. Variation in reserpine concentration in Rauwolfia vomitoria I. Species diversity
B. Greater amphibian richness in the Western Ghats than Eastern Ghats II. Ecological diversity
C. Deserts, mangroves, and coral reefs of India compared to Norway III. Genetic diversity at the biochemical level
D. Over 50,000 genetically different cultivars of rice in India IV. Genetic diversity at the strain level

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze active chemical variation in Rauwolfia vomitoria
The medicinal plant Rauwolfia vomitoria growing in different Himalayan ranges exhibits variations in the potency and concentration of the active chemical reserpine, which exemplifies genetic diversity expressed at the biochemical level within a single species.

Step 2: Analyze amphibian richness differences
Comparing the amphibian richness between the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats evaluates the variety and abundance of different species present in a taxonomic group, representing species diversity.

Step 3: Analyze ecosystem varieties between countries
India possesses an extensive array of distinct ecosystem types including alpine meadows, mangroves, coral reefs, and deserts, far exceeding the habitat varieties found in a Scandinavian nation such as Norway, which defines ecological diversity.

Step 4: Analyze agricultural crop variety in India
India harbors more than 50,000 distinct genetic strains of rice, which demonstrates extensive intraspecific genetic diversity at the strain and cultivar level.

Step 5: Final conceptual conclusion
Synthesizing these concepts connects chemical variation in Rauwolfia vomitoria with genetic diversity at the biochemical level, greater amphibian richness in the Western Ghats with species diversity, broad ecosystem variety in India with ecological diversity, and 50,000 rice strains with genetic diversity at the strain level. Therefore, the correct combination pairs A with III, B with I, C with II, and D with IV.

answer.text: A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MATCH_LIST_Q04 - The evil quartet causes and textbook examples

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Biodiversity Loss Event) List II (Cause from 'The Evil Quartet')
A. Amazon rainforest clearance for cultivating soya beans I. Over-exploitation
B. Extinction of passenger pigeon and Steller's sea cow II. Alien species invasion
C. Decline of native river catfishes due to Clarias gariepinus III. Habitat loss and fragmentation
D. Disappearance of monophagous parasites upon host fish extinction IV. Co-extinction

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Assess clearance of tropical rainforests
The clearing and fragmented destruction of the Amazon rainforest for agricultural conversion to soya bean plantations or grazing pasture represents habitat loss and fragmentation, which is the primary driver of species extinctions.

Step 2: Assess historical extinctions caused by excessive harvesting
The extinction of both the passenger pigeon and Steller's sea cow occurred because human demands transitioned from sustainable utilization to excessive over-hunting and harvest, exemplifying over-exploitation.

Step 3: Assess introduction of non-native catfishes
The illegal introduction of the African catfish Clarias gariepinus for aquaculture poses a grave survival hazard to indigenous catfishes in Indian rivers through competitive displacement and predatory pressures, representing an alien species invasion.

Step 4: Assess compulsory dependence between hosts and associates
When an obligate host fish species is lost, the specialized parasite assemblage that relies strictly upon it inevitably disappears as well, which directly illustrates co-extinction.

Step 5: Final conceptual conclusion
Pairing each event with its corresponding component from 'The Evil Quartet' indicates that clearing the Amazon rainforest corresponds to habitat loss and fragmentation, the extinction of the passenger pigeon corresponds to over-exploitation, the threat from Clarias gariepinus corresponds to alien species invasion, and the loss of dependent host parasites corresponds to co-extinction. Therefore, the correct combination pairs A with III, B with I, C with II, and D with IV.

answer.text: A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MATCH_LIST_Q05 - Prominent ecologists and their key scientific contributions

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Scientist / Ecologist) List II (Major Contribution / Hypothesis)
A. Edward Wilson I. Species-area relationship described by a rectangular hyperbola
B. Robert May II. Rivet popper hypothesis illustrating the effect of species loss on ecosystems
C. Alexander von Humboldt III. Popularized the term 'biodiversity' across all levels of biological organization
D. Paul Ehrlich IV. Conservative global species diversity estimate of about 7 million

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify Edward Wilson's contribution
The sociobiologist Edward Wilson popularized the collective term 'biodiversity' to describe the combined heterogeneity across all biological organization tiers, ranging from intracellular macromolecules to biomes.

Step 2: Identify Robert May's contribution
Robert May formulated a mathematically conservative and scientifically robust estimate placing the global species diversity of Earth at approximately 7 million species.

Step 3: Identify Alexander von Humboldt's contribution
During extensive explorations in South American jungles, the German naturalist Alexander von Humboldt observed that species richness increases with explored area up to a limit, establishing the hyperbolic species-area relationship.

Step 4: Identify Paul Ehrlich's contribution
Stanford ecologist Paul Ehrlich proposed the 'rivet popper hypothesis', using the analogy of an airplane losing rivets to explain how cumulative or critical species extinctions jeopardize ecosystem stability and functioning.

Step 5: Final conceptual conclusion
Correlating each ecologist with their designated contribution shows that Edward Wilson popularized the term biodiversity, Robert May proposed the 7 million species estimate, Alexander von Humboldt formulated the species-area relationship, and Paul Ehrlich developed the rivet popper hypothesis. Therefore, the correct combination pairs A with III, B with IV, C with I, and D with II.

answer.text: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MATCH_LIST_Q06 - Sacred groves and their respective Indian states

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Sacred Grove Tract) List II (State / Geographic Region)
A. Khasi and Jaintia Hills I. Rajasthan
B. Aravalli Hills II. Meghalaya
C. Western Ghat regions III. Madhya Pradesh
D. Sarguja, Chanda, and Bastar areas IV. Karnataka and Maharashtra

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Locate the Khasi and Jaintia sacred groves
The sacred groves of the Khasi and Jaintia Hills are located in Meghalaya; these tracts represent the final refuge for numerous exceptionally rare and threatened endemic plant taxa.

Step 2: Locate the Aravalli Hills sacred groves
The sacred groves conserved along the ancient Aravalli Hills range are located in Rajasthan.

Step 3: Locate the Western Ghat sacred tracts
The biodiversity-rich sacred groves situated along the Western Ghats mountain strip span the states of Karnataka and Maharashtra.

Step 4: Locate the Sarguja, Chanda, and Bastar sacred tracts
The forested sacred groves of Sarguja, Chanda, and Bastar are located within the forested tracts of Madhya Pradesh and adjoining central Indian regions.

Step 5: Final conceptual conclusion

Therefore, the correct combination pairs A with II, B with I, C with IV, and D with III.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MATCH_LIST_Q07 - Species area slope values and global estimates

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Ecological Parameter / Metric) List II (Numerical Value / Range)
A. Value of \(Z\) (regression coefficient) for regional areas (e.g., plants in Britain) I. 0.6 to 1.2
B. Value of \(Z\) when species-area relationship is analyzed across entire continents II. 22 percent
C. Value of \(Z\) for frugivorous birds and mammals in tropical forests of continents III. 0.1 to 0.2
D. Proportion of total global species discovered and cataloged according to May's estimate IV. 1.15

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Determine the regression slope for regional taxonomic assessments
Ecologists have determined that for compact regional scales, such as birds in California or plants in Britain, the regression slope coefficient \(Z\) strictly falls within the narrow range of 0.1 to 0.2 regardless of taxonomic affinity.

Step 2: Determine the regression slope across entire continents
When the species-area relationship is analyzed over vast spatial scales such as entire continental landmasses, the regression slope becomes significantly steeper, giving \(Z\) values ranging between 0.6 and 1.2.

Step 3: Determine the specific slope for tropical frugivores
For specialized feeding guilds like frugivorous (fruit-eating) birds and mammals inhabiting tropical forests across different continents, the calculated slope \(Z\) is steep and equals exactly 1.15.

Step 4: Determine the fraction of recorded global species
According to the scientifically sound global estimate of 7 million total species proposed by Robert May, only slightly more than 1.5 million species have been formally described, meaning that only 22 percent of all living species on Earth have been cataloged so far.

Step 5: Final conceptual conclusion
Aligning each parameter with its established numerical benchmark confirms that regional \(Z\) values span 0.1 to 0.2, continental \(Z\) values span 0.6 to 1.2, tropical frugivore \(Z\) equals 1.15, and the cataloged fraction of global species is 22 percent. Therefore, the correct combination pairs A with III, B with I, C with IV, and D with II.

answer.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MATCH_LIST_Q08 - Latitudinal locations and their avian species richness

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Geographic Location and Latitude) List II (Recorded Number of Bird Species)
A. Colombia (located near the equator) I. 56 species
B. India (having much of its land in tropical latitudes) II. Nearly 1,400 species
C. New York (located at \(41^\circ\text{ N}\)) III. 105 species
D. Greenland (located at \(71^\circ\text{ N}\)) IV. More than 1,200 species

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate avian diversity at the equator
Colombia, situated in the equatorial tropical belt where solar insolation is maximal and climatic stability is high, harbors nearly 1,400 species of birds.

Step 2: Evaluate avian diversity in India
India, with a predominant portion of its geographical landmass situated within warm tropical latitudes, supports an exceptionally high avian diversity of more than 1,200 species.

Step 3: Evaluate avian diversity in temperate regions
As latitude increases away from the equator into temperate zones, species richness declines steadily; thus, New York at \(41^\circ\text{ N}\) supports only 105 species of birds.

Step 4: Evaluate avian diversity in polar regions
In harsh, high-latitude subpolar environments characterized by severe seasonality and low productivity, species numbers drop severely; thus, Greenland at \(71^\circ\text{ N}\) supports merely 56 species of birds.

Step 5: Final conceptual conclusion
This pattern directly exemplifies the latitudinal gradient of biodiversity, where richness decreases from equator to poles: Colombia supports nearly 1,400 bird species, India supports more than 1,200 bird species, New York supports 105 bird species, and Greenland supports 56 bird species. Therefore, the correct combination pairs A with II, B with IV, C with III, and D with I.

answer.text: A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MATCH_LIST_Q09 - Taxonomic proportions and species threatened with extinction

questiontext.text:

D. Share of the world's total land area possessed by India IV. No more than 22 percent

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the representation of insects among animals
Insects represent the most species-rich taxonomic group on Earth, accounting for more than 70 percent of all documented animal species (meaning 7 out of every 10 animals are insects).

Step 2: Analyze the representation of plants among all described life forms
All plant taxa collectively (including algae, fungi, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms, and angiosperms) comprise no more than 22 percent of all recorded living species.

Step 3: Analyze extinction vulnerability among amphibians
Amphibians are exceptionally vulnerable to global environmental degradation and habitat loss, with 32 percent of all amphibian species currently facing the threat of extinction worldwide.

Step 4: Analyze India's global land coverage
India occupies only 2.4 percent of the global terrestrial land area, yet sustains an impressive 8.1 percent share of global species diversity, ranking it among the 12 mega-diversity nations.

Step 5: Final conceptual conclusion
Connecting each global statistic with its accurate value confirms that insects constitute more than 70 percent of animals, all plants comprise no more than 22 percent of total species, amphibians facing extinction threat stand at 32 percent, and India's share of world land area is 2.4 percent. Therefore, the correct combination pairs A with III, B with IV, C with I, and D with II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MATCH_LIST_Q10 - Conservation arguments and ecological hypothesis concepts

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Conservation Argument / Ecological Analogy) List II (Underlying Concept or Example)
A. Narrowly utilitarian I. Ecosystem services like oxygen production by the Amazon forest and insect pollination
B. Broadly utilitarian II. Critical loss of key species that drive major ecosystem functions
C. Ethical argument III. Direct economic exploitation through bioprospecting for pharmaceuticals and timber
D. Rivet on the wing of the airplane IV. Acknowledging that every species has intrinsic value regardless of economic utility

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Detail the narrowly utilitarian justification
The narrowly utilitarian rationale focuses on direct and tangible economic goods humans extract from biodiversity, such as food, construction materials, tannins, industrial resins, and bioprospecting for new medicinal drugs.

Step 2: Detail the broadly utilitarian justification
The broadly utilitarian argument highlights broad ecosystem services provided free of charge by nature, such as large-scale photosynthetic oxygen release by the Amazon basin, climate regulation, soil erosion control, and animal-mediated pollination.

Step 3: Detail the ethical justification
The ethical perspective emphasizes that every co-inhabiting organism possesses intrinsic worth and a philosophical right to exist, imposing a moral obligation on humanity to safeguard all species irrespective of direct economic value.

Step 4: Detail the wing rivet analogy
In Paul Ehrlich's rivet popper hypothesis, rivets securing the wings of the airplane symbolize keystone species whose removal poses an immediate and catastrophic threat to overall ecosystem functioning and structural integrity.

Step 5: Final conceptual conclusion
Matching these conservation principles shows that narrowly utilitarian corresponds to direct economic benefits and bioprospecting, broadly utilitarian corresponds to ecosystem services like oxygen release and pollination, ethical argument corresponds to intrinsic value of species, and the wing rivet corresponds to key species driving major ecosystem functions. Therefore, the correct combination pairs A with III, B with I, C with IV, and D with II.

answer.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Extinction threat percentage across major taxa

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following taxonomic groups in ascending order based on the percentage of their species currently facing the threat of extinction worldwide according to the IUCN:

(I) Mammals
(II) Birds
(III) Amphibians
(IV) Gymnosperms

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The question requires ordering four major taxonomic groups (Mammals, Birds, Amphibians, and Gymnosperms) in ascending order (lowest percentage to highest percentage) according to the proportion of their species facing global extinction threat documented by the IUCN.

Step 2: Identify the documented extinction threat percentage for each taxon
According to the IUCN Red List statistics presented in the textbook:
- Birds: 12 percent of all bird species face the threat of extinction.
- Mammals: 23 percent of all mammal species face the threat of extinction.
- Gymnosperms: 31 percent of all gymnosperm species face the threat of extinction.
- Amphibians: 32 percent of all amphibian species face the threat of extinction.

Step 3: Compare and arrange in ascending order
Comparing the numerical threat values:
12 percent (Birds) < 23 percent (Mammals) < 31 percent (Gymnosperms) < 32 percent (Amphibians).

Step 4: Formulate the sequence
Replacing each taxon with its respective numeral yields the sequence: (II) followed by (I), then (IV), and finally (III).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Birds exhibit the lowest vulnerability among the four groups at 12 percent, whereas amphibians exhibit the highest vulnerability at 32 percent, confirming that the proper ascending order is Birds → Mammals → Gymnosperms → Amphibians, corresponding to the sequence (II) → (I) → (IV) → (III).

answer.text: (II) → (I) → (III) → (IV)
(II) → (I) → (IV) → (III)
(I) → (II) → (IV) → (III)
(IV) → (II) → (I) → (III)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Chronological sequence of global biodiversity milestones

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following international environmental summits, reports, and target commitments in the correct chronological sequence (from earliest to latest):

(I) The historic Convention on Biological Diversity ('The Earth Summit') held in Rio de Janeiro
(II) Release of the IUCN Red List documenting the extinction of 784 species over the preceding 500 years
(III) The World Summit on Sustainable Development held in Johannesburg, South Africa
(IV) Target year committed by 190 countries to achieve a significant reduction in the rate of biodiversity loss

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The task requires arranging four major global conservation milestones and commitments described in the chapter in chronological order from earliest to latest based on their documented calendar years.

Step 2: Determine the calendar year for each milestone
- The Earth Summit (Convention on Biological Diversity) in Rio de Janeiro was held in the year 1992.
- The World Summit on Sustainable Development in Johannesburg, South Africa, took place ten years later in the year 2002.
- The publication of the IUCN Red List documenting 784 recent extinctions was released in the year 2004.
- During the Johannesburg summit in 2002, 190 participating nations pledged their commitment to achieve a significant reduction in biodiversity loss by the target year 2010.

Step 3: Arrange the events chronologically
Ordering by calendar year:
1992 (The Earth Summit) → 2002 (World Summit in Johannesburg) → 2004 (IUCN Red List 2004) → 2010 (Pledged commitment target year).

Step 4: Formulate the sequence
Associating each date with its designated numeral yields the progression: (I) in 1992, followed by (III) in 2002, then (II) in 2004, and concluding with (IV) in 2010.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Verifying the chronological timeline confirms that the Earth Summit occurred first (1992), followed by the Johannesburg Summit (2002), the IUCN Red List publication (2004), and the pledged target year (2010). Thus, the correct sequence is (I) → (III) → (II) → (IV).

answer.text: (I) → (II) → (III) → (IV)
(III) → (I) → (II) → (IV)
(I) → (III) → (II) → (IV)
(I) → (III) → (IV) → (II)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MCQ_Q01 - Popularisation of the term biodiversity

generalfeedback.text:

Step 2: Evaluate the contribution of the named scientist. Edward Wilson, a sociobiologist, popularised the term 'biodiversity' to describe this combined diversity across all organizational levels.

Step 3: Contrast with other ecologists mentioned in the text. Alexander von Humboldt described the species-area relationship, Paul Ehrlich proposed the rivet popper hypothesis, and Robert May estimated global species richness.

The sociobiologist who popularised the term is Edward Wilson.

Alexander von Humboldt
Paul Ehrlich

Step 3: Identify the phenotypic manifestation of this genetic diversity. The variation is expressed in the synthesis of its active medicinal chemical, reserpine, specifically affecting its concentration and medicinal potency.

Step 4: Eliminate irrelevant morphological traits. Features such as petal coloration or vascular bundle arrangements are not the diagnostic variations highlighted for this species.

The genetic variation is manifested as differences in the potency and concentration of the active chemical reserpine.

Step 4: Conclude that biodiversity operates across all levels of biological organisation from macromolecules within cells to biomes.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MCQ_Q15 - Estimated undiscovered species in India

Step 3: Calculate the total projected fauna: \(\text{Total animals} = \frac{90,000}{0.22} \approx 409,090\). Undiscovered animals \(= 409,090 - 90,000 \approx 319,090\), which is more than 3,00,000.

Fewer than 10,000 plant species and 20,000 animal species
More than 1,00,000 plant species and more than 3,00,000 animal species
Exactly 50,000 plant species and 1,00,000 animal species

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MCQ_Q19 - Latitudinal gradient in species diversity

questiontext.text: What general pattern of biodiversity is observed as one moves from the equator towards the polar regions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Define the latitudinal gradient pattern of biodiversity.

Step 2: Biodiversity is not uniformly distributed over the planet.

Step 3: In general, species richness is highest in equatorial and tropical regions (latitudes 23.5° N to 23.5° S) and progressively declines as one travels towards higher temperate and polar latitudes.

Step 4: Conclude that species diversity decreases from the equator towards the poles.

Species diversity generally decreases as one moves away from the equator towards the poles.

answer.text: Species diversity increases steadily from the equator towards the poles
Species diversity remains completely uniform across all latitudes
Species diversity generally decreases from the equator towards the poles

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MCQ_Q23 - Tropical diversity hypothesis evolutionary time

questiontext.text: According to evolutionary biologists, how does historical time account for the greater biological diversity observed in tropical latitudes compared to temperate ones?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the evolutionary time hypothesis explaining tropical diversity.

Step 2: Speciation is generally a function of time. Temperate and polar latitudes experienced recurrent severe glaciations throughout Earth's recent geological past, disrupting ecosystems and eliminating species.

Step 3: In contrast, tropical latitudes remained relatively warm, stable, and undisturbed for millions of uninterrupted years, allowing species uninterrupted evolutionary time to diversify.

Step 4: Conclude that long undisturbed evolutionary time in the tropics promoted greater species diversification.

Tropical latitudes remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years, providing a long evolutionary time for species diversification.

answer.text: Tropical regions were repeatedly glaciated, driving rapid mutation and mass evolutionary transitions
Temperate zones are millions of years older than equatorial tropical landmasses
Unlike temperate regions subjected to frequent glaciations in the past, tropical latitudes remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years, allowing prolonged evolutionary time for speciation
Frequent catastrophes in the tropics repeatedly created empty niches for immediate colonisation

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MCQ_Q24 - Tropical diversity hypothesis niche specialisation

questiontext.text: How does the nature of tropical environments facilitate niche specialisation and high species richness?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the ecological hypothesis regarding environmental constancy.

Step 2: Temperate climates exhibit strong seasonal extremes (harsh winters and hot summers), favouring broad physiological tolerance and generalist habits.

Step 3: Tropical environments are less seasonal, relatively constant, and predictable in temperature, moisture, and day length.

Step 4: Such stable conditions allow species to partition resources finely and develop narrow niche specialisations, accommodating more species in the same community.

Tropical environments are less seasonal, relatively more constant and predictable, promoting niche specialisation.

answer.text: Tropical environments exhibit severe unpredictable climatic fluctuations that force organisms to become generalists
Tropical regions have prolonged freezing winters that select exclusively for specialized hibernating taxa
Tropical environments have low nutrient availability, which prevents competitive exclusion between dominant species
Tropical environments are less seasonal, relatively more constant and predictable, which promotes narrow niche specialisation

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MCQ_Q25 - Tropical diversity hypothesis solar energy

questiontext.text: Which of the following propositions connects solar insolation to the elevated biodiversity of tropical regions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review the productivity hypothesis for tropical diversity.

Step 2: Tropical latitudes receive more direct and abundant solar radiation throughout the year compared to higher latitudes.

Step 3: Higher solar energy input drives elevated rates of photosynthesis and higher primary productivity in tropical plant communities.

Step 4: Higher base productivity supports larger food webs and larger populations, which indirectly fosters and maintains greater species diversity.

Greater solar energy in the tropics contributes to higher productivity, which in turn contributes indirectly to greater species diversity.

answer.text: Greater solar energy availability in the tropics leads to higher primary productivity, which indirectly contributes to greater species diversity
Intense solar radiation causes high lethal mutation rates that instantly double the number of surviving species
High solar radiation prevents primary producers from growing, thereby opening niches for exotic decomposers
Solar energy prevents herbivores from consuming vegetation, resulting in unlimited biomass accumulation

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MCQ_Q26 - Humboldt species area relationship hyperbola

questiontext.text: Alexander von Humboldt observed that within a region, species richness increases with increasing explored area up to a limit. On a normal linear scale, what is the mathematical curve describing this relationship?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify Alexander von Humboldt's pioneering findings from South American wilderness explorations.

Step 2: Humboldt established that species richness increases as the sampled geographical area increases, but the rate of addition gradually slows down, leveling off at larger areas.

Step 3: Plotted on standard arithmetic coordinates, the curve forms a rectangular hyperbola.

Step 4: Its algebraic expression is \(S = C A^Z\), where \(S\) is species richness, \(A\) is area, \(C\) is the Y-intercept, and \(Z\) is the regression coefficient.

The species-area relationship on a normal scale is a rectangular hyperbola described by \(S = C A^Z\).

answer.text: A straight line with a negative slope given by \(S = C - Z A\)
A rectangular hyperbola given by \(S = C A^Z\)
A bell-shaped Gaussian distribution curve
A sigmoid logistic curve given by \(S = \frac{K}{1 + e^{-rA}}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MCQ_Q27 - Logarithmic species area equation parameters

questiontext.text: When the species-area relationship is plotted on a logarithmic scale, the resulting linear equation is \(\log S = \log C + Z \log A\). In this equation, what does '\(Z\)' represent?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Examine the logarithmic transformation of the power function \(S = C A^Z\).

Step 2: Taking logarithms on both sides yields: \(\log S = \log C + Z \log A\).

Step 3: In the standard linear form \(y = c + m x\), \(\log S\) is the dependent variable, \(\log A\) is the independent variable, \(\log C\) is the Y-intercept, and \(Z\) is the slope of the line, also known as the regression coefficient.

Step 4: Conclude that \(Z\) represents the slope of the line or regression coefficient.

In the equation \(\log S = \log C + Z \log A\), \(Z\) represents the slope of the line (regression coefficient).

answer.text: Y-intercept of the logarithmic line
Total species richness of the region
Slope of the line (regression coefficient)
Total geographic area explored

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MCQ_Q28 - Z slope value for regional areas

answer.text: The slope becomes much steeper, with \(Z\) values falling in the range of 0.6 to 1.2

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MCQ_Q31 - Tilman plot diversity and stability findings

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review David Tilman's empirical outdoor ecological experiments.

Step 2: Tilman sought to determine whether species richness directly affects ecosystem stability and functioning.

Step 3: His findings revealed two critical outcomes: first, plots with higher species richness showed significantly less year-to-year variation in total community biomass; second, increased species diversity contributed directly to higher overall productivity.

Step 4: Conclude that higher diversity reduces biomass variation and increases productivity.

Plots with more species showed less year-to-year variation in total biomass and contributed to higher productivity.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MCQ_Q32 - Attributes of a stable biological community

questiontext.text: According to ecological consensus, which of the following combinations of attributes defines a stable biological community?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the defined characteristics of biological community stability.

Step 2: An ecologically stable community must not show excessive fluctuation in annual primary productivity from year to year.

Step 3: It must display either resistance (ability to withstand) or resilience (ability to recover rapidly from) occasional natural or human-induced disturbances.

Step 4: It must also demonstrate resistance against invasions by alien or exotic species.

A stable community shows low productivity variation, disturbance resistance or resilience, and resistance to alien species invasions.

answer.text: High year-to-year variation in productivity, rapid turnover of dominant species, and high susceptibility to exotic invaders

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MCQ_Q33 - Ehrlich rivet popper hypothesis analogies

Step 1: Understand Paul Ehrlich's rivet popper hypothesis analogy.

Step 2: In this conceptual model, an airplane is constructed from thousands of rivets holding all components together.

Step 3: The airplane symbolizes the entire ecosystem, while the individual rivets symbolize the species inhabiting that ecosystem.

Step 4: Passengers removing rivets to take home symbolizes humans driving species to extinction.

The airplane represents the ecosystem, and the rivets represent the individual species.

answer.text: The airplane represents the ecosystem, and the rivets represent the individual species

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_MCQ_Q34 - Rivet popper hypothesis rivets on wings

generalfeedback.text:

answer.text: Rivets on the wings represent introduced alien species that have no functional role in flight
